failure_summary: render_decision.requiredSet forces `you-immediate` (c1r5, role “the single square where YOU can make four next move”, truthBoard afterPlayed) into an L6 “you lost a win AND handed them theirs” story where that square is neither lost nor the opponent’s, and the afterPlayed threat list additionally asserts a false “double at c1r5 (you, window c1r5·c2r6)” — visualize_board on 4222425326433430153304516651020 shows c1r5 as <X> gravity-top for YOU with solver score +2 for the opponent in column 1 (they block and win), so it is not a fork; all 3 runs resolved the contradiction by re-attributing c1r5 to the opponent or calling it given up (A4/G1), and 2/3 additionally dropped the column-2 name after the handle-completion retry (A6) — PRODUCTION-FIDELITY run on gpt-5.4-mini, so the A6/A7b half cannot be separated from model capability.
notes: Only 3 runs present in this answers file (run_index 0-2); mechanical keys |D|3 and |D|4 do not exist. A7e: N/A on every run — trigger requires an OPPONENT gravity-top four on the after-played board; visualize_board 4222425326433430153304516651020 lists only col1 row5 (X) [GT] and col2 row6 (X), both the players own, so no opponent mate-in-1. A5b N/A (player===1). A7c N/A: no *-fork-pivot handle exists in render_decision.zones.aliases. A4 run 0: “you gave up an immediate threat at column 1, row 5” is board-false — the played move CREATED that threat (<X> gravity-top at c1r5 on the after-played board; the render own tactics list says “immediate at c1r5 (you)”). A4 run 1: “let your opponent open a path to a next-move four-in-a-row threat on the square they can use right away” — c1r5 is the movers threat, not the opponents. A3 run 1: the decisive half (the opponents parity win completing at c2r6 along c2r6-c3r6-c4r6-c5r6, verified on opponentPunishment.finalMovestring 4222425326433430153304516651020014066611 where O 40 lands at c2r6) is never named; the only tactic named is the mis-attributed c1r5. A7b run 0: after the guard stripped the c2r6 span (guardDiagnostics failures [P6:raw_coordinate:c2r6], strippedSpecs [c2r6]) the served phrase is the bare “the square at column 2”, which cannot resolve between c2r5 (your fork square) and c2r6 (the shared square that also completes the OPPONENTs row-6 line) — the two have opposite meaning and the link text itself distinguishes lower vs upper square in column 2. A7b runs 1-2: the better column is never named at all (the column that..., the other column) so no referent resolves; run 2 additionally calls the same square both “the square where you can make four next move” and the square the opponent answers with. G1 all runs: served string contradicts the rendered afterPlayed tactics list and the you-immediate role. G2 run 1: guardrail “name both lines with their horizons” not honored — the opponents line is never named, only “their own win”. G5 runs 0-1: rendered afterPlayed entry “double at c1r5 (you, window c1r5·c2r6)” is not board-true as a double threat — the opponent to move plays column 1, blocks c1r5, and the after-played solver row gives that column +2 for them; c2r6 also needs column 2 to fill to row 6. G7 run 1: [zone:c1r5] (handle you-immediate) wraps “the square they can use right away” — opposite of its stated role. G7 run 2: [term:double_threat] is anchored on [zone:c2r6] (you-major, a single completing square on the decision board), but the prompt requires double_threat to be pointed at with you-double or you-future-fork; c2r6 is a lone major threat on the decision board, not a fork. G7 run 0 passes on the SERVED string (the mis-bound [zone:c2r6]the square at c2r5[/zone:c2r6] was stripped by the guard before serving); annotationRepairs empty on all runs. Step 0b done: PROMPT (assembleGroundedPrompt(buildReasonRenderModel(fv))) does contain “Better move: column 2 (lands at c2r4)” verbatim and the correct “immediate at c1r5 (you)” line, so neither the A6 nor the c1r5 failure is information suppression. Retry note: retry_fired=true on all 3 runs for missing required handles; attempt1 of runs 0 and 2 DID name “column 2”, and the retried answers of runs 1 and 2 lost it — the handle-completion retry regressed A6.
